title: Prove centre Gram degree and least invariant scalar-cache bounds
body:
This proves two scoped limits for the historical actual 112-port centre query. The [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c8c48ef5a497ffd7f7e778434c1f074b7b777a03/research/centre-polynomial-cache-limits/PROOF.md), [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c8c48ef5a497ffd7f7e778434c1f074b7b777a03/research/centre-polynomial-cache-limits/SOURCES.json), and [independent agent review](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c8c48ef5a497ffd7f7e778434c1f074b7b777a03/research/centre-polynomial-cache-limits/review/REVIEW.md) give the exact models. Neither result changes the complete kappa calculation.

First, the doubled centre Gram has scalar minimal-polynomial degree at least 409 at every positive tensor size. A scalar-polynomial inverse of `aI+bA`, when it exists and `b != 0`, therefore has degree at least 408. This rules out shorter scalar-polynomial decoder identities for this operator. It does not bound general ADD circuits, matrix-valued encodings, rational expressions, or native decoder cost.

Second, the least scalar cache that contains a query and is invariant under given diagonal updates has dimension equal to the sum of the query's ranks on the joint diagonal fibers. A basis on each fiber attains this dimension. For the pinned query, the specified normal-character family needs 56 rows, while six specified coordinate characters already need all 112 source directions. This gives an exact cache-size test. It assumes a common scalar input representation and does not supply or price native access, cache preparation, storage, or restoration.

The base is [cef4b52f2a59009865bf8eabde1be3f159063703](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/cef4b52f2a59009865bf8eabde1be3f159063703). The consumed historical supplier is pinned at `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; its [archive and contributor lineage](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c8c48ef5a497ffd7f7e778434c1f074b7b777a03/research/centre-polynomial-cache-limits/NOTICE.md) are preserved. [PR #1719](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1719) supplied the doubled port representation. [PR #4720](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4720) already retained the actual query and its separate source-span theorem. [PR #4750](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4750) supplied a fixed-code invariance test. The new cache theorem gives the least invariant enlargement; those predecessor results are not claimed again.

From the repository root, with Python and NumPy, use a new output path:

```sh
env OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python3 -I -B research/centre-polynomial-cache-limits/replay.py --out /tmp/centre-polynomial-cache-replay
```

Expected final line:

```text
PASS_CENTRE_POLYNOMIAL_CACHE_LIMITS
```

The new replay passed under Python 3.14.7 and NumPy 2.5.4. The producer and separate sparse-operator reviewer agree on all 817 moments and the nonzero 409-by-409 Hankel determinant, 2984 modulo 65537. The reviewer checks all 57,344 Bell columns. Exact rational cache checks reproduce the dimension sequences and all 512 character ranks. Duplicate-row, duplicate-column, removed-cache-row, changed-moment, and changed-interface controls passed. The [review receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c8c48ef5a497ffd7f7e778434c1f074b7b777a03/research/centre-polynomial-cache-limits/review/REVIEW.json) includes source binding, a separate forward query reconstruction, and signed-integer overflow bounds.

The infinite-size and least-cache claims follow from written proofs, not finite samples alone. No full supplier, selected-frontier, outer-kappa, or proof-kernel check is claimed. Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance was used; the independent review is by a separate agent, not a human. The remaining native implementation and composition obligations are explicit in the proof guide.
